title: Tame local actions have regular fixed quotients and coinvariant cotangent spaces
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], with residue field $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a finite group acting on $R$ by local ring automorphisms, inducing the identity on $k$, and assume $|H|$ is invertible in $k$. Let $I_H\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be the ideal generated by $h(a)-a$ for all $h\in H$ and $a\in R$. Put $T=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, regarded as a $k$-vector space with its induced $H$-action, and $D_H=\operatorname{span}_k\{h(v)-v:h\in H,v\in T\}$. Then $R/I_H$ is a regular local ring. The canonical surjection $T\to(\mathfrak m/I_H)/(\mathfrak m/I_H)^2$ has kernel exactly $D_H$, and hence induces a canonical isomorphism $T/D_H\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathfrak m/I_H)/(\mathfrak m/I_H)^2$. No coefficient field, completeness, smoothness, or generic freeness is assumed.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.2 and its proof, printed pp.76--77; cotangent consequence explicitly recalled in VIII Lemma 4.2.3, printed p.119.

proof.text: Write $I=I_H$ and $n=|H|$. Since $n$ has nonzero residue, it is a unit of the local ring $R$; its inverse is fixed by every automorphism. Define the additive averaging operator $E(a)=n^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}h(a)$. Reindexing the sum gives $gE=E=Eg$, $E^2=E$, and $E(ca)=cE(a)$ for invariant $c$. Because the residue action is trivial, $a-E(a)\in\mathfrak m$ for every $a$. Thus $h(a)-a=h(a-E(a))-(a-E(a))$: the generators of $I$ may all be taken with $a\in\mathfrak m$. Also $I$ and $\mathfrak m I$ are $H$-stable, since $g(h(a)-a)=(ghg^{-1})(g(a))-g(a)$.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.2, pp.76--77, local coinvariant ideal and tame averaging; elementary calculation written by Q28 instead of completion/linearization.

proof.text: For $u,v\in\mathfrak m$, the identity $g(uv)-uv=g(u)(g(v)-v)+(g(u)-u)v$ puts this difference in $\mathfrak m I$. Every element of $\mathfrak m^2$ is a finite sum of such products, so $g(y)-y\in\mathfrak m I$ for every $y\in\mathfrak m^2$. Consequently $E(y)-y\in\mathfrak m I$ for all $y\in\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.2, local ideal setup; Q28 product calculation on the square of the maximal ideal.

proof.text: For a generator with coefficient $a(h(b)-b)$ of $I$, $a-E(a)\in\mathfrak m$ implies $a(h(b)-b)\equiv E(a)(h(b)-b)\pmod{\mathfrak m I}$. Averaging preserves $\mathfrak m I$ by step 1, and $E(E(a)(h(b)-b))=E(a)(E(h(b))-E(b))=0$. By additivity, $E(z)\in\mathfrak m I$ for every $z\in I$. If also $z\in\mathfrak m^2$, step 2 gives $z-E(z)\in\mathfrak m I$, hence $z\in\mathfrak m I$. The reverse inclusion follows from $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, proving $I\cap\mathfrak m^2=\mathfrak m I$. Thus $I/\mathfrak m I\to T$ is injective. Its image is $D_H$: by step 1 every ideal generator is a difference of elements of $\mathfrak m$, and reduction of its coefficient modulo $\mathfrak m$ gives precisely the stated $k$-span.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.2 and VIII Lemma 4.2.3, cotangent conclusion; Q28 explicit coefficient-averaging calculation.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $T$ is finite dimensional of dimension $d=\dim R$. Choose a basis of $D_H$ and lift it to $x_1,\ldots,x_c\in I$ using step 3. That step identifies their classes with a basis of $I/\mathfrak m I$. Regularity includes Noetherianity [def-weil-regular-scheme], so $I$ is finite; [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] applied to $M=I$ gives $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$. Extend their independent classes in $T$ to a basis by lifts $x_{c+1},\ldots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$. Applying the same Nakayama statement to the finite module $M=\mathfrak m$ shows that the full list generates $\mathfrak m$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] applies to this $d$-element generating list and gives that $R/I=R/(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$ is regular local. Empty lists $c=0$ or $d=0$ are included.

The quotient $R/I$ has maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$ and the same residue field $k$, since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Multiplying representatives gives $(\mathfrak m/I)^2=(\mathfrak m^2+I)/I$. Therefore the canonical map from $T$ onto its cotangent space has kernel $(I+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2$, which is the image of $I$ in $T$ and hence $D_H$ by step 3. Explicitly, $v+D_H\mapsto v+(I+\mathfrak m^2)$ is the required isomorphism; its inverse sends the class of any $u\in\mathfrak m$ to $(u+\mathfrak m^2)+D_H$. Changing $u$ by an element of $I+\mathfrak m^2$ leaves this class unchanged by the kernel equality. These mutually inverse maps prove the canonical cotangent assertion.

lean.statement: theorem tame_fixed_local_regularity (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] (σ : H →* (R ≃+* R)) (hres : ∀ (h : H) (a : R), residue R (σ h a) = residue R a) (htame : IsUnit (Nat.card H : ResidueField R)) : fixedActionIdeal R H σ ≤ maximalIdeal R ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ fixedActionIdeal R H σ) ∧ ∃ f : CotangentSpace R →ₗ[ResidueField R] fixedActionQuotientCotangent R H σ, (∀ x : maximalIdeal R, f ((maximalIdeal R).toCotangent x) = ((maximalIdeal R).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (fixedActionIdeal R H σ))).toCotangent ⟨Ideal.Quotient.mk (fixedActionIdeal R H σ) x, Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ x.property⟩) ∧ Function.Surjective f ∧ LinearMap.ker f = fixedActionCotangentRelations R H σ ∧ ∃ e : (CotangentSpace R ⧸ fixedActionCotangentRelations R H σ) ≃ₗ[ResidueField R] fixedActionQuotientCotangent R H σ, ∀ v : CotangentSpace R, e (Submodule.Quotient.mk v) = f v
